newsitem.title: FRANCE: FIGURE SKATING-TOP MEN LOOKING FOR GREAT IMPROVEMENT.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-TOP MEN LOOKING FOR GREAT IMPROVEMENT.

text.p: The leading men of European figure skating will be seeking considerable improvement from the qualifying round when the main event begins on Wednesday.

Olympic champion Alexei Urmanov had the highest marks and won one of the two qualifying groups on Sunday despite crashing heavily trying a quadruple jump and then scaling down a triple axel to a double.
Russian team mate Alexei Yagudin also fluffed a quad and the coach of both skaters, Alexei Mishin, wants better things in the men's short programme on Wednesday.
"Their performances were not the best way to prepare for the main event, so I am not completely satisfied," said Mishin.

At least both skaters are known to be on good form. Urmanov won two events in the winter's Champions Series, in which he is the titleholder, while Yagudin was second and third in his two counting events.
Philippe Candeloro does not have that base of confidence to take into the short programme, despite his second-place group finish on Sunday.
Candeloro only returned to skating in November after an ankle injury and has only a seventh place at the NHK Trophy in Japan as competitive background coming into this event.
He avoided major errors on Sunday as he placed second in the other group after not attempting a quad.

But he was not surprised the others tried it in the qualifying. "It is because we all know we will need it at next winter's Olympics in Nagano," he said, adding that he intended to work on a quad of his own in the coming weeks.

He said he approached the qualifying "as a training session without all the elements" but he knows he needs a solid performance in the short programme after dropping virtually out of medal contention in last year's European and world championship events following poor showings in the first section.
Titleholder Viacheslav Zagorodniuk of Ukraine also messed up a quad attempt while his predecessor as champion, Russian Ilya Kulik, made several errors and achieved only three triples.
The most satisfied medal contender after qualifying was the surprise winner of the second group, 22-year-old Ukrainian Evgeny Pliuta.
The tall, blond 22-year-old from Kiev did six triples and had only one small error in his routine.
